subject.title: Feature Request: Abstract file scanning pipeline as Memory Plugin API

question: Should OpenClaw add a public memory file-ingestion SDK seam that delivers configured memory scan/watch events to the active memory plugin, and what trust-boundary, chunking, and deletion contract should it expose?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API shape and local-file trust boundary are maintainer product and security choices rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design guarded SDK seam
options.body: Add a documented file-ingestion contract with explicit plugin opt-in, file scope, event semantics, stale cleanup, security review, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Keep helpers only
options.body: Leave list/read helpers as the supported surface and document that memory plugins must own their own watcher, diffing, and cleanup behavior.

options.title: Defer behind broader memory backend design
options.body: Keep this issue open as an API design item until maintainers settle the related memory backend/provider abstraction.

recommendation.title: Design guarded SDK seam
recommendation.body: Add a documented file-ingestion contract with explicit plugin opt-in, file scope, event semantics, stale cleanup, security review, and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The memory engine/plugin and memory host SDK refactor history makes steipete the strongest routing owner for this API boundary decision.
